subtopics.title: Recognising a Cube When You See One

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY perfect cubes?
In x³ + 8 written as a³ + b³, what are a and b?
Why do the common-factor, difference-of-squares and trinomial methods all fail on x³ + 8?
options: The terms share only 1, the expression is a SUM of non-squares, and there is no middle term — only the cubes identity fits
They fail only because 8 is even
They do not fail — squares would work

questions.question: Which expression is ALSO a perfect cube?

subtopics.title: The Identity and the SOAP Mnemonic

questions.question: In SOAP, the three letters that control the signs stand for:
The three TERMS of the long bracket are built in the fixed order:
options: Cube the first, halve the middle, cube the last
Square the first, multiply the pair, square the last
Multiply the pair, square the first, square the last
Double the first, multiply the pair, double the last

questions.question: When (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) is expanded, why does only a³ + b³ remain?
options: The expansion is defined that way by convention
−a²b cancels +a²b and +ab² cancels −ab² — the interior terms wipe each other out

questions.question: The full factorisation of x³ + 8 is:
A learner writes the long bracket of x³ + 8 as x² − 4x + 4. What went wrong?
options: The middle term is a × b = 2x; the learner squared the 2 instead of multiplying it by x
The first term should be x³

questions.question: Why does x² − 2x + 4 stay exactly as it is in the final answer?
options: Because it cancels against the short bracket
No pair of numbers has product 4 and sum −2 — the quadratic factor of a cubes identity never factorises at this level
Because examiners do not read that far

subtopics.title: The Difference Twin and the Full Method

questions.question: x³ − 64 factorises as:
To factorise 5x³ − 40 fully, the correct FIRST move is:
options: Take out the common factor 5, revealing 5(x³ − 8), then apply the cubes identity
Apply the cubes identity directly to 5x³ and 40

questions.question: How do the shapes of the answers to x² − 16 and x³ − 64 differ?
options: Squares give two linear brackets; cubes give one linear and one quadratic bracket, and the quadratic stays
Squares give a quadratic bracket that stays

questions.question: What check should close every cubes factorisation?
options: Substitute x = 1 into the answer only
Compare the answer with the squares identity
Expand the brackets and confirm the middle terms cancel back to the original two terms
No check is needed — identities cannot go wrong

subtopics.title: Cubes Are Just Boxes You Can Stack

questions.question: Which number does NOT belong on the list of six perfect cubes?
Why is y⁹ a perfect cube?
options: Because y³ stacked three times over builds it — the block being cubed is y³
Because every power of y is a cube

questions.question: Two terms joined by a plus, no common factor, no squares anywhere. What is the signal?
options: The expression cannot be factorised at all
Use the difference of squares anyway
Test whether each term is something cubed — this is cubes-identity territory

questions.question: In x³ + 8, the two 'names' that build the entire answer are:

subtopics.title: Three Signs, One Bar of Soap

questions.question: The skeleton of the LONG bracket is built by:
options: Squaring the first name, multiplying the two names, squaring the last name
Adding the two names three times

questions.question: SOAP assigns the three signs as:
Multiplying (x + 2)(x² − 2x + 4) back out leaves only x³ + 8 because:
options: −2x² cancels +2x², and +4x cancels −4x — the four middle products settle in pairs
The middle products are simply left out

questions.question: The middle term of the long bracket for x³ + 8 is −2x and NOT −4x because:
options: The middle position multiplies the two names (x × 2); it never squares the second one
4x would make the bracket too long
2x is always the middle term of every factorisation

subtopics.title: The Curtain, the Twin and Knowing When to Stop

questions.question: Running SOAP on x³ − 64 gives:
'Pulling the curtain' on 5x³ − 40 means:
options: Taking out the common factor 5 to reveal 5(x³ − 8)

questions.question: Why must x² + 4x + 16 be left exactly as it stands?
options: Because the short bracket absorbs it
No pair of numbers multiplies to 16 and adds to 4 — the long bracket never breaks at this level
Because the question ran out of marks

questions.question: What tells you to reach for the squares method instead of the cubes method?
options: The exponent — 'squared' calls squares, 'cubed' calls cubes
Whether the numbers are big or small
Whether the first term contains x
The sign between the terms only
